findings.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) Vulnerability (CVE-2026-82316)
findings.summary_md: SolarWinds lists CVE-2026-82316 as a CVSS 9.1 critical TOCTOU flaw in Serv-U, credited to the Intigriti Bug Bounty Program. The advisory says a user with domain administrator or higher privileges can access or modify protected files outside the intended directory, potentially leading to code execution, with lower risk on Windows. Affected software is Serv-U 2026.3 and below and the fixed release is 2026.4. The page gives a first published date of 11/24/2026 without a time.

findings.title: Serv-U 2026.4 release notes
findings.summary_md: The release notes, dated November 24, 2026, list 18 SolarWinds CVEs and 11 third-party CVEs fixed in Serv-U 2026.4. Nine SolarWinds issues are rated 9.1 critical, including TOCTOU flaws CVE-2026-82315, CVE-2026-82316 and CVE-2026-82319, IDOR escalation CVE-2026-82322, type confusion CVE-2026-82320 and CVE-2026-82321, and Linux root or privilege escalation issues CVE-2026-123167, CVE-2026-123172 and CVE-2026-123168. Most of the 18 are credited to the Intigriti Bug Bounty Program. The notes also record the move to OpenSSL 3.5 LTS and a change that prevents MFA one-time passcodes from being written to log files.

findings.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Flaw Allows Root Escalation on Linux Systems
findings.summary_md: tl;dr daily news reports that SolarWinds disclosed CVE-2026-123172, a CVSS 9.1 privilege escalation in Serv-U that can grant root on Linux installations through 2026.3. It says Windows risk is lower and that upgrading to Serv-U 2026.4 is the mitigation. The article discloses that it was written with AI assistance from a single CVE feed source, so it is useful mainly as an early timestamp for the disclosure.

findings.title: NVD CVE record for CVE-2026-82316
findings.summary_md: NVD published the SolarWinds-supplied record for CVE-2026-82316 at 17:18 UTC on November 24, 2026. It describes a TOCTOU flaw where a domain administrator or higher can access or modify protected files outside the intended directory, potentially leading to code execution, with lower risk in Windows installations. The CVSS 3.1 vector is network accessible, low complexity, high privileges required, no user interaction, changed scope and high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact, scored 9.1.
